I've been putting off this one for quite a while now. Up until today, when you replied to a comment in a thread, your browser sent a request to the server to submit a new comment. If everything went okay, your comment was inserted into database and your browser was instructed to reload the entire page in order to display your newly submited comment.

This method was in no way optimal and wasted bandwidth as well as made the whole process slower.

As of today (I tested this myself but there may be unexpected consequences), when you write a new reply to a comment, your browser will submit the reply and then instruct your browser to only load the comment you just submitted, keeping the rest of the loaded page in tact. Once the browser receives a HTML render of the comment you posted, it is instructed through javascript to simply append your comment to the comment where it belongs.

This uses less bandwidth by only loading relevant parts and makes the entire process faster.

I hope you guys will notice the change and of course, if you (fingers crossed) should notice something unusual about this when replying to comments (remember, only replying to comments was changed, replying to submissions still uses the old method), please report it by replying here.

Thank you!
